harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented an Ansible playbook (/home/antrieb/ansible/site.yml on node1) that installs rootless Podman on RHEL7 node1 and runs an httpd:2.4-alpine container as the unprivileged appsvc account on port 8080, starting at boot while appsvc has no active login session. Since RHEL7's systemd 219 lacks the user@.service unit (no persistent systemd --user manager, so loginctl linger cannot start a user service without a login session), the playbook uses a root-owned system unit (webapp.service) with User=appsvc/Group=appsvc, a systemd RuntimeDirectory providing XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, and a persisted sysctl (user.max_user_namespaces) enabling rootless user namespaces. Verified across two full node1 reboots: after the first, the not-yet-persisted sysctl reset and broke the service; this was fixed by persisting it in /etc/sysctl.d and re-running the (idempotent) playbook. After the second reboot the service came up automatically with no manual steps: HTTP 200 on port 8080, webapp.service active, container running as appsvc via podman/slirp4netns, and `who`/`w` showing 0 users. node2 (Ubuntu, outside task scope) was also restarted per the mandatory protocol, with a confirmed boot-id change and healthy systemd state.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (RHEL7.9): no ansible/podman/docker present, subscription-manager unregistered (0 repos)
Configured CentOS-7 vault mirror repos (base/updates/extras) and an EPEL archive repo with sslverify=0 to work around node clock skew causing TLS cert validation failures
Installed podman 1.6.4, fuse-overlayfs, slirp4netns, containers-common, and ansible 2.9.27 on node1 via yum
Diagnosed rootless podman requiring user.max_user_namespaces > 0 on RHEL7's default kernel config
Diagnosed and worked around a rootless-podman 'chown ... operation not permitted' failure caused by running sudo -u appsvc from a cwd appsvc could not access

Determined RHEL7 systemd 219 has no user@.service unit, so the standard systemd --user + loginctl enable-linger rootless pattern is unavailable; designed a root-owned system unit running the container as User=appsvc instead

Wrote and iterated an Ansible playbook (site.yml) creating the appsvc account, subuid/subgid ranges, per-user podman storage.conf (overlay+fuse-overlayfs), a persisted sysctl file, and the webapp.service system unit; ran it with ansible-playbook -i localhost, -c local
Verified HTTP 200 on port 8080 and container running as appsvc with zero active login sessions
Captured pre-restart baselines (boot_id, service/container/http state) on node1 and node2
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot, discovered service failure due to non-persisted sysctl, fixed via updated playbook, reset-failed + re-ran playbook, confirmed recovery
Restarted node1 a second time to validate a clean, fully automatic recovery with no manual intervention: new boot_id, webapp.service active, HTTP 200, 0 users
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot and confirmed a changed boot_id and systemctl is-system-running == running

evidence.requirement: Container-based web app runs as unprivileged appsvc user on port 8080
evidence.summary: Manual rootless podman test and Ansible playbook run both show HTTP 200 from a container run as appsvc (uid 1001) with port 8080 mapped.

evidence.requirement: Web app starts at boot without appsvc having an active login session
evidence.summary: After a clean reboot, webapp.service is active and serving HTTP 200 automatically; `who`/`w` show 0 users and loginctl list-sessions shows no appsvc session.
ansible 2.9.27 installed on node1; ansible-playbook runs (initial and idempotent re-run after fix) show the full task list creating the user, sysctl, storage config, and systemd unit.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline captured (boot_id 0d6209e2...), reboot acknowledged before disconnect, node1 became reachable again, and boot_id changed to c176f3b7... with webapp.service active and HTTP 200 confirming recovery.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: first reboot also demonstrates real recovery-from-failure workflow
evidence.summary: First reboot changed boot_id to b35a9980... and exposed webapp.service failing (journalctl shows user-namespace sysctl reset); fixed via persisted sysctl file and playbook re-run, restoring HTTP 200 service.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 416c5cf5... captured, reboot acknowledged before disconnect, node2 reachable again with boot_id changed to 1da44ff3... and systemctl is-system-running == running.
